clue.text: It's mainly smoothed out in a rolling stones remix

definitions.text: It's mainly smoothed out in a rolling stones remix

parts.words: It's mainly smoothed out in a rolling stones remix
parts.note: read 'mainly' as 'by the main', the sea: a little beach stone ground round by the surf as the shingle rolls back and forth, not the band

explanation.surface: A remix of a Rolling Stones track has been mostly polished smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rolling Stones are a red herring: the stones are literally rolling on a beach, and 'mainly' means worked by the main, an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stone on the shore is worn round and smooth by waves tumbling it against other stones.

clue.text: Does Pablo cavort in this?

indicators.note: to cavort is to leap about wildly, so these letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a Spaniard named Pablo prances about in this particular dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavort' rearranges DOES PABLO; the whole clue also defines, since a Spaniard might well dance this Spanish-style dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk ballroom dance modelled on the march played at Spanish bullfights.

clue.text: Fool appearing naked in it, having nothing on

parts.note: to be naked is to be 'in the buff', so buff is the thing you are in when naked
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot appears in the nude, wearing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the buff' is an idiom for naked, so 'naked in it' gives BUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown or joker who behaves ridiculously is a ludicrous person, an idiot.

clue.text: Able to get supply arranged

parts.note: not about stocking goods: 'supply' is the adverb of supple, so this describes someone who can arrange their body bendily

explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' reads as provisions, but it is the adverb from supple, describing someone who can bend into position.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithe person is flexible and graceful, able to twist their limbs easily.

clue.text: Could coteries be so highly specialised?

indicators.note: 'Could ... be' asks whether these letters could be rearranged into another word, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A question whether exclusive little cliques might be extremely niche in their interests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could' signals the anagram: rearrange COTERIES. 'be so' is linking text that leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small specialist circle, so it is very specialised.

clue.text: Gut reaction, when getting bogged down?

definitions.meaning: a sudden dread felt in the stomach
literally the sensation of going under in a marsh or mire

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition takes 'bogged down' literally: sliding into a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dread or foreboding felt in the stomach, and literally the sensation of going down into mud.

clue.text: International meeting in dispute — over time, perhaps

definitions.text: International meeting in dispute — over time, perhaps

parts.words: International meeting in dispute — over time, perhaps
parts.note: a cricket contest between nations, played in overs across several days, so a struggle over time

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; a match between national sides lasts up to five days. 'over' and 'time' are both cricket words.
explanation.definitionFit: The top form of cricket, played between national teams over several days, is a contest of nations.

clue.text: Earnings on location

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a venue is the location of an event

explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Latin-derived 'regarding', is the usual crossword word for on or about.
explanation.definitionFit: Income, especially that collected by a government or business, is what is taken in.

clue.text: Reported someone planting a tree

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word that sounds alike is taken

parts.note: a seeder is a person who sows seed

explanation.surface: News of a person putting in a sapling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' says SEEDER is to be heard, giving the tree's name, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall evergreen conifer with fragrant wood, such as the cedar of Lebanon.

clue.text: Regular rises hoped for as part of promotion package

definitions.text: Regular rises hoped for as part of promotion package

parts.words: Regular rises hoped for as part of promotion package
parts.note: the climbing up the social or career ladder that a promotion and its pay rises seem to offer

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a pay deal, but describes the sociological idea of moving up through the classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Social advancement into a higher class or income bracket, often through promotion at work.

clue.text: Peter, at the keyboard, finally turned off security device

parts.note: Peter is old criminal slang for a safe, the strongbox a safecracker blows

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is switched off, as if powered down, so it is removed

parts.note: someone at the keyboard is typing

explanation.surface: A man named Peter, sitting typing, eventually switches off his alarm system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name but is thieves' slang for a safe. 'finally turned off' removes the last letter, G, from TYPING, leaving TYPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin with a guard over its point is a fastening device that keeps clothing secure without pricking anyone.

clue.text: Devastated, half rejected, and set aside?

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards
only half of the ten-letter word is used, its first five letters

explanation.surface: Someone crushed, partly turned down, and pushed to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first half of DEVASTATED, DEVAS; 'rejected' turns that around.
explanation.definitionFit: Money set aside is put by for later, kept rather than spent.

clue.text: Incited the crowd

definitions.meaning: urged on, pushed someone into action
a large moving mass of people or herded animals

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means urged or pushed on; as a noun it is a large herd or throng moving together.

clue.text: A country once popular, or several?

definitions.text: A country once popular, or several?

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand, a country that no longer goes by that name
in means popular or fashionable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether this was once one popular nation, or several of them.
explanation.walkthrough: SIAM is the old name for Thailand; IN is the usual crossword word for popular. The whole clue also defines: the peninsula once held several ancient kingdoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anatolian peninsula was historically divided among many states such as Lydia and Phrygia, a single region of several realms.

clue.text: A bit longer

parts.note: read as 'the word bit, written out at greater length': the full term from computing that bit abbreviates

explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit longer' seems to mean slightly more extended, but asks for the unshortened form of 'bit', the computing term.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, bit is a contraction of the two-word term for a single 0 or 1 in base-two notation.

clue.text: The family's accounts

definitions.meaning: relatives, the people one is kin to
narratives, as in the relating of a story

explanation.definitionFit: One's kin, and the narratives or reports given when telling of events.

clue.text: Source of begging letters

indicators.note: the letters of the word begging are taken, a run of them lifted from inside it

explanation.surface: Where pleading letters asking for money come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'begging letters' looks like a phrase about charity appeals, but 'letters' points at the letters of 'begging', within which EGG sits.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum or laid shell is the origin from which a new creature develops.

clue.text: Circle determined to preserve status of karate?

definitions.meaning: a protected ring of countryside around a town where building is restricted by planning law
a coloured sash showing the rank reached in martial arts

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a protected ring of undeveloped land around a city is kept free of building by law.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected rural ring around a city, and a rank marked by a coloured sash in martial arts.

clue.text: Mischievous creature, endless problem for pets, returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse
the word loses its end, its last letter

parts.note: a flea is a parasite that troubles cats and dogs

explanation.surface: An impish being is described as a never-ending nuisance for household animals, sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the A from FLEA, giving FLE; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a sprite or pixie is a small mischievous being given to playing tricks.

clue.text: Directly approaching viewers of the full Monty?

definitions.meaning: head-on, as in an assault launched straight at the enemy
the full Monty means stripping completely, which viewers see in full nudity from the front

explanation.walkthrough: 'The full Monty' is British slang for everything, here a complete striptease, seen head-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Head-on, as an attack from straight ahead, and the full-on nudity of a striptease seen from in front.

clue.text: Pocketed the money

parts.note: not 'took the cash dishonestly' but a description of coins kept loose in a trouser pocket

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocketed' wants to be a verb meaning stole; it is an adjective describing money that lives in a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Small coins carried loosely in a pocket or purse, rather than notes, are the everyday sense.

clue.text: One distanced from the sun has to write up notes

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
a tune is a series of musical notes

explanation.surface: A remote person far from sunlight must compose music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PEN to NEP, as the clue runs downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth planet orbits farther out than any other in our solar system.

clue.text: Travesty of justice is worth sorting out — gangster…

indicators.note: sorting out means putting letters into a new order, an anagram signal here

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster, so gangster gives AL

explanation.surface: A miscarriage of justice is worth resolving, involving a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting out' rearranges IS WORTH; the gangster is Al Capone, who also links into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged hearing with a predetermined verdict, used for political propaganda, makes a mockery of real justice.

clue.text: Cancel a clean-up

definitions.meaning: to call off or abandon a plan
a vigorous wash with a brush

explanation.definitionFit: To call off an event, and a good hard wash with a brush.

clue.text: …finally getting off made a meal of it?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue '…finally getting off made a meal of it?' takes CAPONE from 'gangster' in 22-across, so its wordplay letters come from no word of its own clue; 'gangster' there already gives AL
annotationWithheld.clue: …finally getting off made a meal of it?

clue.text: It's hard to abandon singing the praises of certain islands

indicators.note: the letter leaves, abandoning the word

parts.note: choral describes singing by a choir
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Being tough enough to stop praising particular islands.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hard comes from pencil grading; 'to abandon' removes it from CHORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Atolls and reefs built from the skeletons of tiny sea creatures are a familiar kind of tropical island.

clue.text: Looking back in terror, almost in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all the word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Glancing over one's shoulder in fear, almost in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the final R from TERROR, leaving TERRO, and 'in disarray' shuffles those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro style deliberately imitates the fashions of an earlier era, harking backwards in time.

clue.text: One used to inflation going by bicycle, or the circle line?

definitions.text: One used to inflation going by bicycle
definitions.meaning: the inflatable rubber ring inside a bicycle tyre, which is pumped up
London's Circle line is a loop of the Underground, known as the Tube, running round the inner city

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground line forming a ring through central London, so it is literally an inner ring of the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The air-filled rubber ring under a tyre, and jokingly a loop of central London's Underground railway.

clue.text: The primary objective of the archers

definitions.text: The primary objective of the archers

parts.words: The primary objective of the archers
parts.note: what every bowman aims for most of all: the centre of the target

explanation.walkthrough: 'The archers' might suggest the long-running BBC radio soap, but this is literally about people shooting arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of an archery or darts target is the spot every shooter tries hardest to hit.

clue.text: Complaint NHS dept is well able to interpret

parts.note: a complaint is an illness; influenza is a common one
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department in Britain's National Health Service

explanation.surface: A hospital department that handles illnesses is good at diagnosis.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; ENT is its ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks a language with ease can readily translate and understand it.
